extraction.name: FOMO60K
extraction.description: A large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain MRI scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. It includes clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and wide anatomical and pathological variability for self-supervised learning in medical imaging.
extraction.creator: Asbjøm Munk, Stefano Cerri, Jakob Ambsdorf, Julia Machnio, Sebastian Nørgaard Llambias, Vardan Nersesjan, Christian Hedeager Krag, Peirong Liu, Pablo Rocamora García, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi, Mikael Boesen, Michael Eriksen Benros, Juan Eugenio Iglesias, and Mads Nielsen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was aggregated from 16 publicly available sources and derived from publicly available datasets; minimal preprocessing was applied to preserve original image characteristics.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 60,529 brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, including clinical- and research-grade images with multiple MRI sequences.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is heterogeneous but still aggregated from 16 publicly available sources, and the paper notes that existing neuroimaging resources are often curated for specific diseases or patient populations with homogeneous imaging protocols and limited pathological variability; FOMO60K is intended to address these limitations by including clinical- and research-grade images and scans with large brain anomalies.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is intended for self-supervised pretraining and benchmarking in medical imaging at scale; minimal preprocessing was applied to preserve original characteristics, and the paper notes that the dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available. No explicit non-recommended uses are stated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is presented as a resource to lower barriers to entry, facilitate benchmarking and broader adoption of self-supervised learning in medical imaging, and support progress in neuroimaging research.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains brain MRI scans from subjects and sessions, and the paper mentions subject identifiers and source datasets; it does not explicitly discuss collection of demographic sensitive attributes such as gender, age, or socio-economic status in the provided section.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for self-supervised pretraining and fine-tuning/benchmarking of SSL methods in medical imaging. The usage notes state the dataset can be used with no further preprocessing for pre-training, and users are asked to cite the source papers.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available and will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available. No explicit maintainer names or deprecation policy are stated in the provided text.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Minimal preprocessing was applied; MRI preprocessing comprised reorienting images to RAS orientation, affine co-registration, and skull-stripping. For DWI scans stored in 4D format, a b=0 volume was extracted, three diffusion-weighted volumes were selected based on gradient directions, and the corresponding volumes were averaged to produce a single representative 3D image.
